evals.prompt: Can you review this final log extract like a senior engineer before it goes out? BH-7, ground el. 101.20 m, washbore with HW casing. 0.0-0.3 TOPSOIL. 0.3-2.1 SAND, some silt, trace gravel, dense, brown, moist. SS-1 at 0.76-1.37 m blows 2-3-3, recovery 450 mm. SS-2 at 1.52-2.13 m blows 3-4-4 N=8, rec 640 mm. 2.1-5.6 CLAY (CL), some silt, grey, stiff, wet, PP 0.5, 0.75, 0.5 kg/cm2 on SS-3 at 2.29 m. Lab on SS-3: LL 58, PL 24, PI 34, MC 31%. SS-4 at 3.05 m: 50/3" N=50. 5.6 m END OF BOREHOLE, refusal on bedrock. Water level 1.2 m on completion (casing in hole, wash water). Water dry on 24 h.
evals.expected_output: Ranks findings by design impact. Catches: dense sand contradicted by N=6 and N=8 (loose); SS-1 N not reported; SS-2 recovery 640 mm exceeds a 610 mm drive; PP used on a split-spoon sample (not meaningful) and PP of ~0.5-0.75 kg/cm2 implies soft to firm, contradicting stiff; CL symbol contradicts LL 58 (should be CH); refusal 50/3" shown as N=50 without refusal label; bedrock claimed from refusal without proving core; water level taken with wash water in the hole is not a groundwater level, and 'dry at 24 h' conflicts with it; moisture 'wet' for clay above/near water needs comment. Does not flag compact/medium terminology or refusal length as errors.
assertions: Flags that 'dense' contradicts the low SPT N values (N=6 and N=8 indicate loose)
Notes that SS-1 has no N reported (should be 6)
Flags SS-2 recovery 640 mm as exceeding the 610 mm drive length
Flags pocket penetrometer readings taken on a split-spoon (driven) sample as unreliable
Flags that PP readings of about 0.5-0.75 kg/cm2 indicate soft to firm clay, contradicting 'stiff'
Flags CL as inconsistent with LL 58 (should be CH / fat clay)
Flags the 50/3" refusal being reported as a plain N=50 without refusal labelling
Flags 'refusal on bedrock' as unproven without coring
Flags the 1.2 m water level as unreliable because wash water and casing were in the hole, and notes the conflict with 'dry at 24 h'
Does not treat a refusal penetration shorter than the drive length as an error in itself

evals.prompt: Turn this field sheet transcription into final-log descriptions the way a Canadian consultancy would, in metres, and list every interpretation you added so the reviewer can accept or reject it. Depths in feet. 0-4" TOPSOIL. 4"-2' FILL - mix of sandy silt, brick frags, dk brown, moist. 2'-14' CLAY - grey/brown, moist, firm to stiff, HP, tr silt, tr fg sand. 5' - w/ silt, damp. 9' - moist below 9'. 11' - tr gypsum nodules. 14' TILL - tan, moist, MP, f.g. sand, tr gravel, tr cobbles, grinding on cobbles. 19' S.A.A. grey, wet, sat. fg sand pockets. Auger refusal 21.5' on suspected boulder. Misc tests: PP=1.5,1.75,1.5 @ 6' on ST-2; T=0.45 @ 6' (standard head, kg/cm2). No seepage on completion, backfilled with cuttings.
evals.expected_output: Converts depths correctly (4 in = 0.10 m, 2 ft = 0.61 m, 14 ft = 4.27 m, 21.5 ft = 6.55 m). Produces layered descriptions with the main name in capitals, FILL with brick fragments, CLAY with (CH) as an interpretation, within-layer changes as '- ... below x m' sub-lines, a TILL named with its matrix only as a flagged interpretation, S.A.A. resolved, refusal line, numbered completion notes. Converts PP to kPa (qu about 147-172 kPa, Cu about 74-86 kPa) and torvane to Cu about 44 kPa with stated assumptions; notes PP and torvane disagree and which to trust; lists every added interpretation separately.
assertions: Converts depths correctly: 4 in = 0.10 m, 2 ft = 0.61 m, 14 ft = 4.27 m, 21.5 ft = 6.55 m
Keeps FILL as its own layer and mentions the brick fragments
Presents the 5 ft, 9 ft and 11 ft changes as sub-lines within the clay layer at about 1.52 m, 2.74 m and 3.35 m
Converts the pocket penetrometer readings to kPa (qu about 147-172 kPa or Cu about 74-86 kPa) and states the conversion
Converts the torvane reading to about 44 kPa undrained shear strength
Points out that the pocket penetrometer and torvane strengths disagree
Resolves S.A.A. at 19 ft (5.79 m) into the till description with the grey, wet and sand-pocket changes
Ends with an auger refusal line at 6.55 m on a suspected boulder
Includes completion notes for no seepage and backfill with cuttings
Lists the added interpretations (e.g. USCS symbol, till matrix name, density term) separately for reviewer acceptance

evals.prompt: Rock question for the core logging feature: run R3 from 6.10 to 7.60 m, HQ triple tube. The logger wrote pieces (m): 0.22, 0.04, 0.31, 0.09, 0.12 (MB both ends), 0.07, 0.36 and 0.05 lost; fracture sheet has J at 6.32 (35 deg to core axis, rough, Fe stained), MB at 6.36, J at 6.67 (80 deg, smooth, clay infill 2 mm), BCZ 7.05-7.12. Sheet says recovery 1.21 (88%) and RQD 0.85/1.50. Hole is inclined 70 deg from horizontal. What should the app store and show, and is anything on the sheet wrong?
evals.expected_output: Computes TCR = 1.21/1.50 = 81% and flags the sheet's bracketed 88% as inconsistent with its own length. Flags that recovered pieces (1.21) plus lost core (0.05) leave 0.24 m of the 1.50 m run unaccounted for. Explains RQD counts natural-break pieces >= 100 mm with mechanical breaks ignored: rejoining across the mechanical breaks gives 0.22 + 0.35 + 0.28 + 0.36 = 1.21 m (81%), or about 1.14 m (76%) if the 0.07 m piece is really the broken zone; counting the pieces at face value (0.22+0.31+0.12+0.36 = 1.01 m, 67%) is wrong because it treats mechanical breaks as natural. The sheet's 0.85/1.50 (57%) matches no rule and needs the logger to confirm. Also flags that the broken zone at 7.05-7.12 m falls inside the 0.36 m 'intact' piece. Distinguishes angle to core axis from dip and says true dip needs oriented core or a survey. Converts along-hole depth to vertical (x sin 70 deg, e.g. 6.10 m along hole is about 5.73 m vertical) for elevations. Recommends storing lengths as written plus derived percentages, classifies RQD quality (poor to fair/good depending on basis), and calls out the smooth clay-infilled joint as design-relevant.
assertions: Computes total core recovery as about 81% (1.21/1.50) and flags the sheet's 88% as inconsistent
Flags that recovered plus lost core (1.26 m) does not account for the full 1.50 m run
Explains that RQD ignores mechanical breaks and counts natural-break pieces of at least 100 mm
Gives a recomputed RQD (about 67% and/or about 78%) and flags the sheet's 0.85 m (57%) as needing confirmation
Distinguishes the angle to the core axis from true dip and says true dip needs orientation data
Converts along-hole depth to vertical depth using sin 70 degrees
Recommends storing the values as written alongside derived percentages
Calls out the smooth clay-infilled joint as design-relevant

evals.prompt: A new geotech firm from Alberta is onboarding next week. They sent blank field forms showing: depth column in feet only, proportion key 'trace <10%, little 10-20%, some 20-35%, and 35-50%', density terms 'very loose/loose/compact/dense/very dense', a 'Q' column for pocket pen in tsf, a column 'N (bpf)', sample codes SS, ST, BS, CB, and a frozen ground section with codes like Nbn and Vx. What do we need to set up and what should we ask their engineer before we touch the product?
evals.expected_output: Fills a convention profile (feet field units, Burmister-style proportion terms, Canadian density terms, PP in tsf with conversion, bpf meaning a single N per foot vs increments, sample code mapping with unknowns BS and CB flagged, frozen-ground scheme as a specialist extension). Lists gaps the product cannot store yet. Produces a concrete question list (report units, PP conversion and Cu vs qu, whether increments are recorded, refusal display, meaning of BS/CB, frozen ground scheme, sign-off workflow). Asks for field/final pairs. Keeps everything company-agnostic: no firm name in config or code.
assertions: Records that field depths are in feet and raises the reporting-unit question
Identifies the proportion terms as Burmister-style and treats them as a per-organisation setting
Recognises 'compact' as the Canadian equivalent of medium dense
Notes the pocket penetrometer reads in tsf and gives or asks for a conversion to kPa
Asks what 'N (bpf)' means: a single blows-per-foot value versus recorded 150 mm increments
Flags sample codes BS and CB as unknown and to be confirmed
Recognises Nbn and Vx as frozen-ground (ASTM D4083 / NRC-style) descriptors and flags them as a product gap
Asks for field and final log pairs from the firm
Keeps the setup company-agnostic (configuration, no firm-specific code or naming)
Produces a concrete list of questions for the firm's engineer
